title: consolidate-sdks-adaptive-retries-stream-callbacks-go-conn-pooling
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Python/TS/Go SDKs: new adaptive retry/backoff defaults and opt-in token-rotation safety checks
- Streaming API: new lean callback-based streaming helpers (backwards-compatible adapters provided)
- Go SDK: HTTP/2 connection pooling and keepalive adjustments to reduce cold-starts
- Version bumps: python 1.14.0, typescript 0.9.3, go v0.7.1
description:
Motivation:
We had small-but-noticeable behavioral diffs across the Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs around transient error handling and streaming ergonomics. Teams building cross-service features saw inconsistent retry timing, and Go clients suffered extra connection churn under high multiplexed loads. This PR consolidates retries, introduces a compact callback-based streaming API for better backpressure control, and fixes Go connection reuse problems.

Summary of changes (single-line commits):
- feat(sdk): introduce adaptive three-tier retryer (exp/backoff/jitter) with token-aware auth guard
- feat(python): add callback_stream helper and compatibility shim for legacy iterator-based streams
- feat(ts): add StreamCallback class + typed helper; update examples and docs
- fix(go): replace naive net/http Transport config with pooled HTTP/2 transport and tune keepalive; add conn reuse tests
- test: add cross-sdk integration tests for 429/503 behavior and streaming concurrency
- docs: migration guide + changelog entries
- ci: flake8 + lint fixes, increase Go race test timeout

Files changed (high level):
- sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py (new helper + shim)
- sdk/python/redwood/retries.py (new adaptive retryer and config)
- sdk/python/CHANGELOG.md (version bump notes)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/callback.ts (new public API)
- sdk/typescript/src/retries.ts (shared retry rules)
- sdk/typescript/examples/streaming-callbacks.ts (updated example)
- sdk/go/client/transport.go (http2 pooling + keepalive changes)
- sdk/go/client/retry.go (retry policy)
- docs/sdk-migration.md (migration guide)
- tests/integration/stream_retry_matrix.test (cross-sdk behavioral tests)

Small illustrative snippet (python streaming shim):
"""python
# adapter for backward compatibility - yields + callback both supported
def callback_stream(request, on_token):
    # underlying transport yields chunks; user supplied on_token invoked per chunk
    for chunk in _transport_stream(request):
        on_token(chunk)
        yield chunk
"""

Compatibility notes:
- The new callback-based streaming helper is opt-in. Iterator-based code continues to work unchanged because we ship a tiny shim that yields the same chunk objects. Migration is recommended for high-concurrency services where explicit callbacks enable better resource control.
- Retry defaults are more aggressive against 429/503 responses but incorporate an auth-rotation guard: after a token-rotation event we temporarily reduce retry amplification to avoid token churn loops. Teams can override via SDK config.

Review conversation (highlights):

- Maya: "Added concurrent stream test + expanded Go race timeout. PTAL."
- Liam: "Two nits: rename RetryPolicy.max_attempts -> max_retries for clarity, and please document the auth-rotation window."
- Maya: "Renamed and added docs with the auth window rationale (see docs/sdk-migration.md)."
- Ravi: "Approves after CI green. Thanks for the thorough cross-sdk tests."

CI status history:
- Initial run: python lint (flake8) failed on formatting; go tests flaked under race detector; TS build passed but a benchmark flaky test was marked unstable.
- Iteration 2: fixed flake8 issues, increased go test timeout and added an explicit sync in transport tests; re-run CI -> all checks passed.

Why this approach:
- Centralizes retry parameters to reduce surprising cross-language differences while keeping opt-out knobs for advanced users.
- Callback streaming reduces GC/iterator pressure for long-lived streams and makes it easier to integrate backpressure and batching on the client side.
- Go connection pooling reduces TLS handshakes and cold-start latencies for bursty workloads.

Upgrade notes for integrators:
- Python users: no required code changes. To use callbacks import callback_stream from redwood.streaming. See examples.
- TypeScript users: StreamCallback is added under sdk package; older iterator helpers still present for compatibility.
- Go users: minor behavior changes in transport timing; strongly recommend bumping to v0.7.1 and running integration tests under your environment.

- Merge method: squash and merge
- Squash summary: consolidated retry + streaming refactor across SDKs; go transport pool; tests + docs
